feature: Fifty tracks and a hundred clips, fourth pass
summary: Zooming and scrolling the timeline of a 50 track edit now fit in a 120 Hz frame, and the hitch at the start of every scroll is gone. Adding a track while it plays is still over one frame.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed. Your copy of the 50 track edit: File > Open (Cmd-Shift-G) ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev/Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz. Measured in the probe with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --wide 50 and --wide 100; numbers in Scripts/perf/baselines/wide-50.json and wide-100.json.

try.do: Open Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz with File > Open.
Pinch the timeline in and out.
Scroll sideways with two fingers, stop, and scroll again.
Scroll down through all the tracks and back up.
Compare with the filmed zoom and scroll: queue/audits/2026-11-25-wide-edit-zoom-scroll.mp4.
Press Space, and add a video track from a track's right-click menu while it plays.

evaluate: Does the timeline keep up with a pinch from start to finish?
Does a sideways scroll start without a hitch?
Does the long edit of your own that lagged feel smooth now?
rough: Main thread a frame, 50 tracks, before this pass / now (bar p95 8.3, none over 16): zoom in p95 10.8 / 6.9, out 10.0 / 7.4, near Fit 9.9 / 6.8, along 5.8 / 5.7, tracks down 5.8 / 4.1. Worst frame along 40 / 9. Over five runs every p95 was under 8.3; three single frames went over 16: one of 21 zooming in, one of 40 near Fit, and one of 17 scrolling along on a build before the last change.
Add track while it plays is not at its bar of 16 ms: 19 to 25, and 12 to 17 for its undo. Every other edit is 9 to 16.
Played end to end: 0 or 1 of 3637 frames dropped in four runs, no clip frame wrong with ten up. Starting play at 0:58 from rest still waits about 727 ms.
Export against the one made before any of this work: 3600 frames, worst frame 100.7 dB (a few dozen pixels off by one level), sound identical.
100 tracks: zoom p95 7.8 to 8.2, along 7.4, up and down 10.4 (17.2 before), 7 of 3637 frames dropped, edits 13 to 35 ms.
VoiceOver and other helper apps see a far track only once it has been scrolled near, as in any long Mac list.
No mock covers a 50 track timeline. The film shows this build only; the before and after side by side is in the second pass's report.
